final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor materially narrowed the position from an overbroad certify-now framing to a policy-bounded claim: certification is supportable only as a qualified decision with explicit disclosure of the unresolved API-migration support limitation unless and until an approved mitigation or risk acceptance exists. That narrowed position can be reached from the same admissible evidence and is consistent with the policy text. No genuinely new admissible evidence was added, so the unresolved operational concerns remain unresolved and must stay accounted for. The change is therefore not based on new proof that the underlying issue was fixed; it is based on the Actor abandoning the unsupported clean-certification implication and aligning the claim to the evidentiary limits. This supports compliant_with_caveats, not compliant.
remaining_concerns: The developer-support migration slice remains below target for a named launch use case, so materiality is still unresolved on the admissible record.

The draft mitigation runbook is still unapproved and lacks required completeness elements such as approver and stop-ship threshold, so it cannot satisfy the policy predicate for removing disclosure obligations.
The current model-card draft still states there are no known material limitations despite the unresolved migration issue and reviewer concern, so record-to-disclosure alignment is still unresolved.

There is still no admissible evidence of final disclosure text, approved risk acceptance, or an approved mitigation record; certification is supportable only if those caveats are actually implemented before launch.
